07.9bb9556bd1:
<n>71:2</n> Deus, iudícium tuum regi da: * et iustítiam tuam fílio regis:
<n>71:2</n> Iudicáre pópulum tuum in iustítia, * et páuperes tuos in iudício.
<n>71:3</n> Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: * et colles iustítiam.
<n>71:4</n> Iudicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: * et humiliábit calumniatórem.
<n>71:5</n> Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, * in generatióne et generatiónem.
<n>71:6</n> Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: * et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.
<n>71:7</n> Oriétur in diébus eius iustítia, et abundántia pacis: * donec auferátur luna.
<n>71:8</n> Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: * et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
07.d6c05ed9cf:
<n>71:2</n> Give to the king thy judgment, O God: * and to the king’s son thy justice:
<n>71:2</n> To judge thy people with justice, * and thy poor with judgment.
<n>71:3</n> Let the mountains receive peace for the people: * and the hills justice.
<n>71:4</n> He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: * and he shall humble the oppressor.
<n>71:5</n> And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, * throughout all generations.
<n>71:6</n> He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; * and as showers falling gently upon the earth.
<n>71:7</n> In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, * till the moon be taken away.
<n>71:8</n> And he shall rule from sea to sea, * and from the river unto the ends of the earth.
07.141477098c:
<n>71:9</n> Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: * et inimíci eius terram lingent.
<n>71:10</n> Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: * reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.
<n>71:11</n> Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: * omnes gentes sérvient ei:
<n>71:12</n> Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: * et páuperem, cui non erat adiútor.
<n>71:13</n> Parcet páuperi et ínopi: * et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.
<n>71:14</n> Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: * et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.
<n>71:15</n> Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: * tota die benedícent ei.
<n>71:16</n> Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus eius: * et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.
<n>71:17</n> Sit nomen eius benedíctum in sǽcula: * ante solem pérmanet nomen eius.
<n>71:17</n> Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: * omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
<n>71:18</n> Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * qui facit mirabília solus:
<n>71:19</n> Et benedíctum nomen maiestátis eius in ætérnum: * et replébitur maiestáte eius omnis terra: fiat, fiat.
07.8cef0d3f6e:
<n>71:9</n> Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: * and his enemies shall lick the ground.
<n>71:10</n> The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: * the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:
<n>71:11</n> And all kings of the earth shall adore him: * all nations shall serve him.
<n>71:12</n> For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: * and the needy that had no helper.
<n>71:13</n> He shall spare the poor and needy: * and he shall save the souls of the poor.
<n>71:14</n> He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: * and their names shall be honourable in his sight.
<n>71:15</n> And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: * they shall bless him all the day.
<n>71:16</n> And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: * and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.
<n>71:17</n> Let his name be blessed for evermore: * his name continueth before the sun.
<n>71:17</n> And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: * all nations shall magnify him.
<n>71:18</n> Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, * who alone doth wonderful things.
<n>71:19</n> And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: * and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.
07.d363067be3:
<n>72:1</n> Quam bonus Israël Deus, * his, qui recto sunt corde!
<n>72:2</n> Mei autem pæne moti sunt pedes: * pæne effúsi sunt gressus mei.
<n>72:3</n> Quia zelávi super iníquos, * pacem peccatórum videns.
<n>72:4</n> Quia non est respéctus morti eórum: * et firmaméntum in plaga eórum.
<n>72:5</n> In labóre hóminum non sunt, * et cum homínibus non flagellabúntur:
<n>72:6</n> Ídeo ténuit eos supérbia, * opérti sunt iniquitáte et impietáte sua.
<n>72:7</n> Pródiit quasi ex ádipe iníquitas eórum: * transiérunt in afféctum cordis.
<n>72:8</n> Cogitavérunt, et locúti sunt nequítiam: * iniquitátem in excélso locúti sunt.
<n>72:9</n> Posuérunt in cælum os suum: * et lingua eórum transívit in terra.
07.cee2a8ea21:
<n>72:1</n> How good is God to Israel, * to them that are of a right heart!
<n>72:2</n> But my feet were almost moved; * my steps had wellnigh slipped.
<n>72:3</n> Because I had a zeal on occasion of the wicked, * seeing the prosperity of sinners.
<n>72:4</n> For there is no regard to their death, * nor is there strength in their stripes.
<n>72:5</n> They are not in the labour of men: * neither shall they be scourged like other men.
<n>72:6</n> Therefore pride hath held them fast: * they are covered with their iniquity and their wickedness.
<n>72:7</n> Their iniquity hath come forth, as it were from fatness: * they have passed into the affection of the heart.
<n>72:8</n> They have thought and spoken wickedness: * they have spoken iniquity on high.
<n>72:9</n> They have set their mouth against heaven: * and their tongue hath passed through the earth.
07.35299a7761:
<n>72:10</n> Ídeo convertétur pópulus meus hic: * et dies pleni inveniéntur in eis.
<n>72:11</n> Et dixérunt: Quómodo scit Deus, * et si est sciéntia in excélso?
<n>72:12</n> Ecce, ipsi peccatóres, et abundántes in sǽculo, * obtinuérunt divítias.
<n>72:13</n> Et dixi: Ergo sine causa iustificávi cor meum, * et lavi inter innocéntes manus meas:
<n>72:14</n> Et fui flagellátus tota die, * et castigátio mea in matutínis.
<n>72:15</n> Si dicébam: Narrábo sic: * ecce, natiónem filiórum tuórum reprobávi.
<n>72:16</n> Existimábam ut cognóscerem hoc, * labor est ante me:
<n>72:17</n> Donec intrem in Sanctuárium Dei: * et intéllegam in novíssimis eórum.
07.2ce915ecba:
<n>72:10</n> Therefore will my people return here * and full days shall be found in them.
<n>72:11</n> And they said: How doth God know? * and is there knowledge in the most High?
<n>72:12</n> Behold these are sinners; and yet abounding in the world * they have obtained riches.
<n>72:13</n> And I said: Then have I in vain justified my heart, * and washed my hands among the innocent.
<n>72:14</n> And I have been scourged all the day; * and my chastisement hath been in the mornings.
<n>72:15</n> If I said: I will speak thus; * behold I should condemn the generation of thy children.
<n>72:16</n> I studied that I might know this thing, * it is a labour in my sight:
<n>72:17</n> Until I go into the sanctuary of God, * and understand concerning their last ends.
07.2aae65ccbe:
<n>72:18</n> Verúmtamen propter dolos posuísti eis: * deiecísti eos dum allevaréntur.
<n>72:19</n> Quómodo facti sunt in desolatiónem, súbito defecérunt: * periérunt propter iniquitátem suam.
<n>72:20</n> Velut sómnium surgéntium, Dómine, * in civitáte tua imáginem ipsórum ad níhilum rédiges.
<n>72:21</n> Quia inflammátum est cor meum, et renes mei commutáti sunt: * et ego ad níhilum redáctus sum, et nescívi.
<n>72:23</n> Ut iuméntum factus sum apud te: * et ego semper tecum.
<n>72:24</n> Tenuísti manum déxteram meam: et in voluntáte tua deduxísti me, * et cum glória suscepísti me.
<n>72:25</n> Quid enim mihi est in cælo? * et a te quid vólui super terram?
<n>72:26</n> Defécit caro mea, et cor meum: * Deus cordis mei, et pars mea Deus in ætérnum.
<n>72:27</n> Quia ecce, qui elóngant se a te, períbunt: * perdidísti omnes, qui fornicántur abs te.
<n>72:28</n> Mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est: * pónere in Dómino Deo spem meam:
<n>72:28</n> Ut annúntiem omnes prædicatiónes tuas, * in portis fíliæ Sion.
07.f5e71c5a19:
<n>72:18</n> But indeed for deceits thou hast put it to them: * when they were lifted up, thou hast cast them down.
<n>72:19</n> How are they brought to desolation? they have suddenly ceased to be: * they have perished by reason of their iniquity.
<n>72:20</n> As the dream of them that awake, O Lord; * so in thy city thou shalt bring their image to nothing.
<n>72:21</n> For my heart hath been inflamed, and my reins have been changed: * and I am brought to nothing, and I knew not.
<n>72:23</n> I am become as a beast before thee: * and I am always with thee.
<n>72:24</n> Thou hast held me by my right hand; and by thy will thou hast conducted me, * and with thy glory thou hast received me.
<n>72:25</n> For what have I in heaven? * and besides thee what do I desire upon earth?
<n>72:26</n> For thee my flesh and my heart hath fainted away: * thou art the God of my heart, and the God that is my portion for ever.
<n>72:27</n> For behold they that go far from thee shall perish: * thou hast destroyed all them that are disloyal to thee.
<n>72:28</n> But it is good for me to adhere to my God, * to put my hope in the Lord God:
<n>72:28</n> That I may declare all thy praises, * in the gates of the daughter of Sion.
07.09d9ae6722:
<n>73:1</n> Ut quid, Deus, repulísti in finem: * irátus est furor tuus super oves páscuæ tuæ?
<n>73:2</n> Memor esto congregatiónis tuæ, * quam possedísti ab inítio.
<n>73:2</n> Redemísti virgam hereditátis tuæ: * mons Sion, in quo habitásti in eo.
<n>73:3</n> Leva manus tuas in supérbias eórum in finem: * quanta malignátus est inimícus in sancto!
<n>73:4</n> Et gloriáti sunt qui odérunt te: * in médio solemnitátis tuæ.
<n>73:5</n> Posuérunt signa sua, signa: * et non cognovérunt sicut in éxitu super summum.
<n>73:6</n> Quasi in silva lignórum secúribus excidérunt iánuas eius in idípsum: * in secúri et áscia deiecérunt eam.
<n>73:7</n> Incendérunt igni Sanctuárium tuum: * in terra polluérunt tabernáculum nóminis tui.
<n>73:8</n> Dixérunt in corde suo cognátio eórum simul: * Quiéscere faciámus omnes dies festos Dei a terra.
<n>73:9</n> Signa nostra non vídimus, iam non est prophéta: * et nos non cognóscet ámplius.
07.c2553d1fc4:
<n>73:1</n> O God, why hast thou cast us off unto the end: * why is thy wrath enkindled against the sheep of thy pasture?
<n>73:2</n> Remember thy congregation, * which thou hast possessed from the beginning.
<n>73:2</n> The sceptre of thy inheritance which thou hast redeemed: * mount Sion in which thou hast dwelt.
<n>73:3</n> Lift up thy hands against their pride unto the end; * see what things the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary.
<n>73:4</n> And they that hate thee have made their boasts, * in the midst of thy solemnity.
<n>73:5</n> They have set up their ensigns for signs, * and they knew not both in the going out and on the highest top.
<n>73:6</n> As with axes in a wood of trees, they have cut down at once the gates thereof, * with axe and hatchet they have brought it down.
<n>73:7</n> They have set fire to thy sanctuary: * they have defiled the dwelling place of thy name on the earth.
<n>73:8</n> They said in their heart, the whole kindred of them together: * Let us abolish all the festival days of God from the land.
<n>73:9</n> Our signs we have not seen, there is now no prophet: * and he will know us no more.
07.aca330414e:
<n>73:10</n> Úsquequo, Deus, improperábit inimícus: * irrítat adversárius nomen tuum in finem?
<n>73:11</n> Ut quid avértis manum tuam, et déxteram tuam, * de médio sinu tuo in finem?
<n>73:12</n> Deus autem Rex noster ante sǽcula: * operátus est salútem in médio terræ.
<n>73:13</n> Tu confirmásti in virtúte tua mare: * contribulásti cápita dracónum in aquis.
<n>73:14</n> Tu confregísti cápita dracónis: * dedísti eum escam pópulis Æthíopum.
<n>73:15</n> Tu dirupísti fontes, et torréntes: * tu siccásti flúvios Ethan.
<n>73:16</n> Tuus est dies, et tua est nox: * tu fabricátus es auróram et solem.
<n>73:17</n> Tu fecísti omnes términos terræ: * æstátem et ver tu plasmásti ea.
07.b77901c782:
<n>73:10</n> How long, O God, shall the enemy reproach: * is the adversary to provoke thy name for ever?
<n>73:11</n> Why dost thou turn away thy hand: and thy right hand * out of the midst of thy bosom for ever?
<n>73:12</n> But God is our king before ages: * he hath wrought salvation in the midst of the earth.
<n>73:13</n> Thou by thy strength didst make the sea firm: * thou didst crush the heads of the dragons in the waters.
<n>73:14</n> Thou hast broken the heads of the dragon: * thou hast given him to be meat for the people of the Ethiopians.
<n>73:15</n> Thou hast broken up the fountains and the torrents: * thou hast dried up the Ethan rivers.
<n>73:16</n> Thine is the day, and thine is the night: * thou hast made the morning light and the sun.
<n>73:17</n> Thou hast made all the borders of the earth: * the summer and the spring were formed by thee.
07.4df5e418d1:
<n>73:18</n> Memor esto huius, inimícus improperávit Dómino: * et pópulus insípiens incitávit nomen tuum.
<n>73:19</n> Ne tradas béstiis ánimas confiténtes tibi, * et ánimas páuperum tuórum ne obliviscáris in finem.
<n>73:20</n> Réspice in testaméntum tuum: * quia repléti sunt, qui obscuráti sunt terræ dómibus iniquitátum.
<n>73:21</n> Ne avertátur húmilis factus confúsus: * pauper et inops laudábunt nomen tuum.
<n>73:22</n> Exsúrge, Deus, iúdica causam tuam: * memor esto improperiórum tuórum, eórum quæ ab insipiénte sunt tota die.
<n>73:23</n> Ne obliviscáris voces inimicórum tuórum: * supérbia eórum, qui te odérunt, ascéndit semper.
07.1f2c05eb40:
<n>73:18</n> Remember this, the enemy hath reproached the Lord: * and a foolish people hath provoked thy name.
<n>73:19</n> Deliver not up to beasts the souls that confess to thee: * and forget not to the end the souls of thy poor.
<n>73:20</n> Have regard to thy covenant: * for they that are the obscure of the earth have been filled with dwellings of iniquity.
<n>73:21</n> Let not the humble be turned away with confusion: * the poor and needy shall praise thy name.
<n>73:22</n> Arise, O God, judge thy own cause: * remember thy reproaches with which the foolish man hath reproached thee all the day.
<n>73:23</n> Forget not the voices of thy enemies: * the pride of them that hate thee ascendeth continually.
07.fcd74d4485:
<n>74:2</n> Confitébimur tibi, Deus: * confitébimur, et invocábimus nomen tuum.
<n>74:3</n> Narrábimus mirabília tua: * cum accépero tempus, ego iustítias iudicábo.
<n>74:4</n> Liquefácta est terra, et omnes qui hábitant in ea: * ego confirmávi colúmnas eius.
<n>74:5</n> Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere: * et delinquéntibus: Nolíte exaltáre cornu:
<n>74:6</n> Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum: * nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem.
<n>74:7</n> Quia neque ab Oriénte, neque ab Occidénte, neque a desértis móntibus: * quóniam Deus iudex est.
<n>74:8</n> Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat: * quia calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto.
<n>74:9</n> Et inclinávit ex hoc in hoc: verúmtamen fæx eius non est exinaníta: * bibent omnes peccatóres terræ.
<n>74:10</n> Ego autem annuntiábo in sǽculum: * cantábo Deo Iacob.
<n>74:11</n> Et ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam: * et exaltabúntur córnua iusti.
07.a10bb2cc16:
<n>74:2</n> We will praise thee, O God: * we will praise, and we will call upon thy name.
<n>74:3</n> We will relate thy wondrous works: * when I shall take a time, I will judge justices.
<n>74:4</n> The earth is melted, and all that dwell therein: * I have established the pillars thereof.
<n>74:5</n> I said to the wicked: Do not act wickedly: * and to the sinners: Lift not up the horn.
<n>74:6</n> Lift not up your horn on high: * speak not iniquity against God.
<n>74:7</n> For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the desert hills: * for God is the judge.
<n>74:8</n> One he putteth down, and another he lifteth up: * for in the hand of the Lord there is a cup of strong wine full of mixture.
<n>74:9</n> And he hath poured it out from this to that: but the dregs thereof are not emptied: * all the sinners of the earth shall drink.
<n>74:10</n> But I will declare for ever: * I will sing to the God of Jacob.
<n>74:11</n> And I will break all the horns of sinners: * but the horns of the just shall be exalted.
07.5f1c606222:
<n>75:2</n> Notus in Iudǽa Deus: * in Israël magnum nomen eius.
<n>75:3</n> Et factus est in pace locus eius: * et habitátio eius in Sion.
<n>75:4</n> Ibi confrégit poténtias árcuum, * scutum, gládium, et bellum.
<n>75:5</n> Illúminans tu mirabíliter a móntibus ætérnis: * turbáti sunt omnes insipiéntes corde.
<n>75:6</n> Dormiérunt somnum suum: * et nihil invenérunt omnes viri divitiárum in mánibus suis.
<n>75:7</n> Ab increpatióne tua, Deus Iacob, * dormitavérunt qui ascendérunt equos.
07.a5ddb57402:
<n>75:2</n> In Judea God is known: * his name is great in Israel.
<n>75:3</n> And his place is in peace: * and his abode in Sion:
<n>75:4</n> There hath he broken the powers of bows, * the shield, the sword, and the battle.
<n>75:5</n> Thou enlightenest wonderfully from the everlasting hills. * All the foolish of heart were troubled.
<n>75:6</n> They have slept their sleep; * and all the men of riches have found nothing in their hands.
<n>75:7</n> At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob, * they have all slumbered that mounted on horseback.
07.76a5d16e5c:
<n>75:8</n> Tu terríbilis es, et quis resístet tibi? * ex tunc ira tua.
<n>75:9</n> De cælo audítum fecísti iudícium: * terra trémuit et quiévit,
<n>75:10</n> Cum exsúrgeret in iudícium Deus, * ut salvos fáceret omnes mansuétos terræ.
<n>75:11</n> Quóniam cogitátio hóminis confitébitur tibi: * et relíquiæ cogitatiónis diem festum agent tibi.
<n>75:12</n> Vovéte, et réddite Dómino, Deo vestro: * omnes, qui in circúitu eius affértis múnera.
<n>75:13</n> Terríbili et ei qui aufert spíritum príncipum, * terríbili apud reges terræ.
07.0daf804718:
<n>75:8</n> Thou art terrible, and who shall resist thee? * from that time thy wrath.
<n>75:9</n> Thou hast caused judgment to be heard from heaven: * the earth trembled and was still,
<n>75:10</n> When God arose in judgment, * to save all the meek of the earth.
<n>75:11</n> For the thought of man shall give praise to thee: * and the remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.
<n>75:12</n> Vow ye, and pay to the Lord your God: * all you that are round about him bring presents.
<n>75:13</n> To him that is terrible, even to him who taketh away the spirit of princes: * to the terrible with the kings of the earth.
07.d829a2be34:
<n>70:1</n> In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me, et éripe me.
<n>70:2</n> Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * et salva me.
<n>70:3</n> Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in locum munítum: * ut salvum me fácias,
<n>70:3</n> Quóniam firmaméntum meum, * et refúgium meum es tu.
<n>70:4</n> Deus meus, éripe me de manu peccatóris, * et de manu contra legem agéntis et iníqui:
<n>70:5</n> Quóniam tu es patiéntia mea, Dómine: * Dómine, spes mea a iuventúte mea.
<n>70:6</n> In te confirmátus sum ex útero: * de ventre matris meæ tu es protéctor meus.
<n>70:7</n> In te cantátio mea semper: * tamquam prodígium factus sum multis: et tu adiútor fortis.
<n>70:8</n> Repleátur os meum laude, ut cantem glóriam tuam: * tota die magnitúdinem tuam.
<n>70:9</n> Ne proícias me in témpore senectútis: * cum defécerit virtus mea, ne derelínquas me.
<n>70:10</n> Quia dixérunt inimíci mei mihi: * et qui custodiébant ánimam meam, consílium fecérunt in unum.
<n>70:11</n> Dicéntes: Deus derelíquit eum, persequímini, et comprehéndite eum: * quia non est qui erípiat.
<n>70:12</n> Deus, ne elongéris a me: * Deus meus, in auxílium meum réspice.
07.58ec46db23:
<n>70:1</n> In thee, O Lord, I have hoped, let me never be put to confusion: * deliver me in thy justice, and rescue me.
<n>70:2</n> Incline thy ear unto me, * and save me.
<n>70:3</n> Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a place of strength: * that thou mayst make me safe.
<n>70:3</n> For thou art my firmament * and my refuge.
<n>70:4</n> Deliver me, O my God, out of the hand of the sinner, * and out of the hand of the transgressor of the law and of the unjust.
<n>70:5</n> For thou art my patience, O Lord: * my hope, O Lord, from my youth.
<n>70:6</n> By thee have I been confirmed from the womb: * from my mother’s womb thou art my protector.
<n>70:7</n> Of thee shall I continually sing: * I am become unto many as a wonder, but thou art a strong helper.
<n>70:8</n> Let my mouth be filled with praise, that I may sing thy glory; * thy greatness all the day long.
<n>70:9</n> Cast me not off in the time of old age: * when my strength shall fail, do not thou forsake me.
<n>70:10</n> For my enemies have spoken against me; * and they that watched my soul have consulted together,
<n>70:11</n> Saying: God hath forsaken him: pursue and take him, * for there is none to deliver him.
<n>70:12</n> O God, be not thou far from me: * O my God, make haste to my help.
07.57742381e4:
<n>70:13</n> Confundántur, et defíciant detrahéntes ánimæ meæ: * operiántur confusióne, et pudóre qui quærunt mala mihi.
<n>70:14</n> Ego autem semper sperábo: * et adíciam super omnem laudem tuam.
<n>70:15</n> Os meum annuntiábit iustítiam tuam: * tota die salutáre tuum.
<n>70:16</n> Quóniam non cognóvi litteratúram, introíbo in poténtias Dómini: * Dómine, memorábor iustítiæ tuæ solíus.
<n>70:17</n> Deus, docuísti me a iuventúte mea: * et usque nunc pronuntiábo mirabília tua.
<n>70:18</n> Et usque in senéctam et sénium: * Deus, ne derelínquas me,
<n>70:18</n> Donec annúntiem brácchium tuum * generatióni omni, quæ ventúra est:
<n>70:19</n> Poténtiam tuam, et iustítiam tuam, Deus, usque in altíssima, quæ fecísti magnália: * Deus, quis símilis tibi?
<n>70:20</n> Quantas ostendísti mihi tribulatiónes multas et malas: et convérsus vivificásti me: * et de abýssis terræ íterum reduxísti me:
<n>70:21</n> Multiplicásti magnificéntiam tuam: * et convérsus consolátus es me.
<n>70:22</n> Nam et ego confitébor tibi in vasis psalmi veritátem tuam: * Deus, psallam tibi in cíthara, Sanctus Israël.
<n>70:23</n> Exsultábunt lábia mea cum cantávero tibi: * et ánima mea, quam redemísti.
<n>70:24</n> Sed et lingua mea tota die meditábitur iustítiam tuam: * cum confúsi et revériti fúerint, qui quærunt mala mihi.
07.dff2df88df:
<n>70:13</n> Let them be confounded and come to nothing that detract my soul; * let them be covered with confusion and shame that seek my hurt.
<n>70:14</n> But I will always hope; * and will add to all thy praise.
<n>70:15</n> My mouth shall shew forth thy justice; * thy salvation all the day long.
<n>70:16</n> Because I have not known learning, I will enter into the powers of the Lord: * O Lord, I will be mindful of thy justice alone.
<n>70:17</n> Thou hast taught me, O God, from my youth: * and till now I will declare thy wonderful works.
<n>70:18</n> And unto old age and grey hairs: * O God, forsake me not,
<n>70:18</n> Until I shew forth thy arm * to all the generation that is to come:
<n>70:19</n> Thy power, and thy justice, O God, even to the highest great things thou hast done: * O God, who is like to thee?
<n>70:20</n> How great troubles hast thou shewn me, many and grievous: and turning thou hast brought me to life, * and hast brought me back again from the depths of the earth:
<n>70:21</n> Thou hast multiplied thy magnificence; * and turning to me thou hast comforted me.
<n>70:22</n> For I will also confess to thee thy truth with the instruments of psaltery: * O God, I will sing to thee with the harp, thou holy one of Israel.
<n>70:23</n> My lips shall greatly rejoice, when I shall sing to thee; * and my soul which thou hast redeemed.
<n>70:24</n> Yea and my tongue shall meditate on thy justice all the day; * when they shall be confounded and put to shame that seek evils to me.
07.e0578af32a:
<n>77:1</n> Atténdite, pópule meus, legem meam: * inclináte aurem vestram in verba oris mei.
<n>77:2</n> Apériam in parábolis os meum: * loquar propositiónes ab inítio.
<n>77:3</n> Quanta audívimus et cognóvimus ea: * et patres nostri narravérunt nobis.
<n>77:4</n> Non sunt occultáta a fíliis eórum: * in generatióne áltera.
<n>77:4</n> Narrántes laudes Dómini, et virtútes eius: * et mirabília eius, quæ fecit.
<n>77:5</n> Et suscitávit testimónium in Iacob: * et legem pósuit in Israël.
<n>77:5</n> Quanta mandávit pátribus nostris nota fácere ea fíliis suis: * ut cognóscat generátio áltera.
<n>77:6</n> Fílii qui nascéntur, et exsúrgent, * et narrábunt fíliis suis.
<n>77:7</n> Ut ponant in Deo spem suam, et non obliviscántur óperum Dei: * et mandáta eius exquírant.
<n>77:8</n> Ne fiant sicut patres eórum: * generátio prava et exásperans.
<n>77:8</n> Generátio, quæ non diréxit cor suum: * et non est créditus cum Deo spíritus eius.
07.db4acb640f:
<n>77:1</n> Attend, O my people, to my law: * incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
<n>77:2</n> I will open my mouth in parables: * I will utter propositions from the beginning.
<n>77:3</n> How great things have we heard and known, * and our fathers have told us.
<n>77:4</n> They have not been hidden from their children, * in another generation.
<n>77:4</n> Declaring the praises of the Lord, and his powers, * and his wonders which he hath done.
<n>77:5</n> And he set up a testimony in Jacob: * and made a law in Israel.
<n>77:5</n> How great things he commanded our fathers, that they should make the same known to their children: * that another generation might know them.
<n>77:6</n> The children that should be born and should rise up, * and declare them to their children.
<n>77:7</n> That they may put their hope in God and may not forget the works of God: * and may seek his commandments.
<n>77:8</n> That they may not become like their fathers, * a perverse and exasperating generation.
<n>77:8</n> A generation that set not their heart aright: * and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
07.8585f87664:
<n>77:9</n> Fílii Ephrem intendéntes et mitténtes arcum: * convérsi sunt in die belli.
<n>77:10</n> Non custodiérunt testaméntum Dei: * et in lege eius noluérunt ambuláre.
<n>77:11</n> Et oblíti sunt benefactórum eius: * et mirabílium eius quæ osténdit eis.
<n>77:12</n> Coram pátribus eórum fecit mirabília in terra Ægýpti: * in campo Táneos.
<n>77:13</n> Interrúpit mare, et perdúxit eos: * et státuit aquas quasi in utre.
<n>77:14</n> Et dedúxit eos in nube diéi: * et tota nocte in illuminatióne ignis.
<n>77:15</n> Interrúpit petram in erémo: * et adaquávit eos velut in abýsso multa.
<n>77:16</n> Et edúxit aquam de petra: * et dedúxit tamquam flúmina aquas.
07.ff2e3ac08a:
<n>77:9</n> The sons of Ephraim who bend and shoot with the bow: * they have turned back in the day of battle.
<n>77:10</n> They kept not the covenant of God: * and in his law they would not walk.
<n>77:11</n> And they forgot his benefits, * and his wonders that he had shewn them.
<n>77:12</n> Wonderful things did he do in the sight of their fathers, in the land of Egypt, * in the field of Tanis.
<n>77:13</n> He divided the sea and brought them through: * and he made the waters to stand as in a vessel.
<n>77:14</n> And he conducted them with a cloud by day: * and all the night with a light of fire.
<n>77:15</n> He struck the rock in the wilderness: * and gave them to drink, as out of the great deep.
<n>77:16</n> He brought forth water out of the rock: * and made streams run down as rivers.
07.a4c5de49a4:
<n>77:17</n> Et apposuérunt adhuc peccáre ei: * in iram excitavérunt Excélsum in inaquóso.
<n>77:18</n> Et tentavérunt Deum in córdibus suis, * ut péterent escas animábus suis.
<n>77:19</n> Et male locúti sunt de Deo: * dixérunt: Numquid póterit Deus paráre mensam in desérto?
<n>77:20</n> Quóniam percússit petram, et fluxérunt aquæ: * et torréntes inundavérunt.
<n>77:20</n> Numquid et panem póterit dare, * aut paráre mensam pópulo suo?
<n>77:21</n> Ídeo audívit Dóminus, et dístulit: * et ignis accénsus est in Iacob, et ira ascéndit in Israël.
<n>77:22</n> Quia non credidérunt in Deo: * nec speravérunt in salutári eius:
<n>77:23</n> Et mandávit núbibus désuper: * et iánuas cæli apéruit.
<n>77:24</n> Et pluit illis manna ad manducándum: * et panem cæli dedit eis.
<n>77:25</n> Panem Angelórum manducávit homo, * cibária misit eis in abundántia.
<n>77:26</n> Tránstulit Austrum de cælo: * et indúxit in virtúte sua Áfricum.
<n>77:27</n> Et pluit super eos sicut púlverem carnes: * et sicut arénam maris volatília pennáta.
<n>77:28</n> Et cecidérunt in médio castrórum eórum: * circa tabernácula eórum.
<n>77:29</n> Et manducavérunt, et saturáti sunt nimis, et desidérium eórum áttulit eis: * non sunt fraudáti a desidério suo.
<n>77:30</n> Adhuc escæ eórum erant in ore ipsórum: * et ira Dei ascéndit super eos.
<n>77:31</n> Et occídit pingues eórum, * et eléctos Israël impedívit.
07.06ab49529e:
<n>77:17</n> And they added yet more sin against him: * they provoked the most High to wrath in the place without water.
<n>77:18</n> And they tempted God in their hearts, * by asking meat for their desires.
<n>77:19</n> And they spoke ill of God: * they said: Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?
<n>77:20</n> Because he struck the rock, and the waters gushed out, * and the streams overflowed.
<n>77:20</n> Can he also give bread, * or provide a table for his people?
<n>77:21</n> Therefore the Lord heard, and was angry: * and a fire was kindled against Jacob, and wrath came up against Israel.
<n>77:22</n> Because they believed not in God: * and trusted not in his salvation.
<n>77:23</n> And he had commanded the clouds from above, * and had opened the doors of heaven.
<n>77:24</n> And had rained down manna upon them to eat, * and had given them the bread of heaven.
<n>77:25</n> Man ate the bread of angels: * he sent them provisions in abundance.
<n>77:26</n> He removed the south wind from heaven: * and by his power brought in the southwest wind.
<n>77:27</n> And he rained upon them flesh as dust: * and feathered fowls like as the sand of the sea.
<n>77:28</n> And they fell in the midst of their camp, * round about their pavilions.
<n>77:29</n> So they did eat, and were filled exceedingly, and he gave them their desire: * they were not defrauded of that which they craved.
<n>77:30</n> As yet their meat was in their mouth: * and the wrath of God came upon them.
<n>77:31</n> And he slew the fat ones amongst them, * and brought down the chosen men of Israel.
07.7922fc7f4a:
<n>77:32</n> In ómnibus his peccavérunt adhuc: * et non credidérunt in mirabílibus eius.
<n>77:33</n> Et defecérunt in vanitáte dies eórum: * et anni eórum cum festinatióne.
<n>77:34</n> Cum occíderet eos, quærébant eum: * et revertebántur, et dilúculo veniébant ad eum.
<n>77:35</n> Et rememoráti sunt quia Deus adiútor est eórum: * et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est.
<n>77:36</n> Et dilexérunt eum in ore suo, * et lingua sua mentíti sunt ei.
<n>77:37</n> Cor autem eórum non erat rectum cum eo: * nec fidéles hábiti sunt in testaménto eius.
<n>77:38</n> Ipse autem est miséricors, et propítius fiet peccátis eórum: * et non dispérdet eos.
<n>77:38</n> Et abundávit ut avérteret iram suam: * et non accéndit omnem iram suam:
<n>77:39</n> Et recordátus est quia caro sunt: * spíritus vadens et non rédiens.
<n>77:40</n> Quóties exacerbavérunt eum in desérto, * in iram concitavérunt eum in inaquóso?
<n>77:41</n> Et convérsi sunt, et tentavérunt Deum: * et Sanctum Israël exacerbavérunt.
07.5ec9b185de:
<n>77:32</n> In all these things they sinned still: * and they believed not for his wondrous works.
<n>77:33</n> And their days were consumed in vanity, * and their years in haste.
<n>77:34</n> When he slew them, then they sought him: * and they returned, and came to him early in the morning.
<n>77:35</n> And they remembered that God was their helper: * and the most high God their redeemer.
<n>77:36</n> And they loved him with their mouth: * and with their tongue they lied unto him:
<n>77:37</n> But their heart was not right with him: * nor were they counted faithful in his covenant.
<n>77:38</n> But he is merciful, and will forgive their sins: * and will not destroy them.
<n>77:38</n> And many a time did he turn away his anger: * and did not kindle all his wrath.
<n>77:39</n> And he remembered that they are flesh: * a wind that goeth and returneth not.
<n>77:40</n> How often did they provoke him in the desert: * and move him to wrath in the place without water?
<n>77:41</n> And they turned back and tempted God: * and grieved the holy one of Israel.
07.0218dddcd3:
<n>77:42</n> Non sunt recordáti manus eius, * die qua redémit eos de manu tribulántis.
<n>77:43</n> Sicut pósuit in Ægýpto signa sua, * et prodígia sua in campo Táneos.
<n>77:44</n> Et convértit in sánguinem flúmina eórum: * et imbres eórum, ne bíberent.
<n>77:45</n> Misit in eos cœnomyíam, et comédit eos: * et ranam, et dispérdidit eos.
<n>77:46</n> Et dedit ærúgini fructus eórum: * et labóres eórum locústæ.
<n>77:47</n> Et occídit in grándine víneas eórum: * et moros eórum in pruína.
<n>77:48</n> Et trádidit grándini iuménta eórum: * et possessiónem eórum igni.
<n>77:49</n> Misit in eos iram indignatiónis suæ: * indignatiónem, et iram, et tribulatiónem: immissiónes per ángelos malos.
<n>77:50</n> Viam fecit sémitæ iræ suæ, non pepércit a morte animábus eórum: * et iuménta eórum in morte conclúsit.
<n>77:51</n> Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra Ægýpti: * primítias omnis labóris eórum in tabernáculis Cham.
<n>77:52</n> Et ábstulit sicut oves pópulum suum: * et perdúxit eos tamquam gregem in desérto.
<n>77:53</n> Et dedúxit eos in spe, et non timuérunt: * et inimícos eórum opéruit mare.
<n>77:54</n> Et indúxit eos in montem sanctificatiónis suæ: * montem, quem acquisívit déxtera eius.
<n>77:54</n> Et eiécit a fácie eórum gentes: * et sorte divísit eis terram in funículo distributiónis.
<n>77:55</n> Et habitáre fecit in tabernáculis eórum: * tribus Israël.
<n>77:56</n> Et tentavérunt, et exacerbavérunt Deum excélsum: * et testimónia eius non custodiérunt.
<n>77:57</n> Et avertérunt se, et non servavérunt pactum: * quemádmodum patres eórum convérsi sunt in arcum pravum.
<n>77:58</n> In iram concitavérunt eum in cóllibus suis: * et in sculptílibus suis ad æmulatiónem eum provocavérunt.
07.21b1380f53:
<n>77:42</n> They remembered not his hand, * in the day that he redeemed them from the hand of him that afflicted them:
<n>77:43</n> How he wrought his signs in Egypt, * and his wonders in the field of Tanis.
<n>77:44</n> And he turned their rivers into blood, * and their showers that they might not drink.
<n>77:45</n> He sent amongst them diverse sorts of flies, which devoured them: * and frogs which destroyed them.
<n>77:46</n> And he gave up their fruits to the blast, * and their labours to the locust.
<n>77:47</n> And he destroyed their vineyards with hail, * and their mulberry trees with hoarfrost.
<n>77:48</n> And he gave up their cattle to the hail, * and their stock to the fire.
<n>77:49</n> And he sent upon them the wrath of his indignation: * indignation and wrath and trouble, which he sent by evil angels.
<n>77:50</n> He made a way for a path to his anger: * he spared not their souls from death, and their cattle he shut up in death.
<n>77:51</n> And he killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt: * the firstfruits of all their labour in the tabernacles of Cham.
<n>77:52</n> And he took away his own people as sheep: * and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.
<n>77:53</n> And he brought them out in hope, and they feared not: * and the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
<n>77:54</n> And he brought them into the mountain of his sanctuary: * the mountain which his right hand had purchased.
<n>77:54</n> And he cast out the Gentiles before them: * and by lot divided to them their land by a line of distribution.
<n>77:55</n> And he made the tribes of Israel * to dwell in their tabernacles.
<n>77:56</n> Yet they tempted, and provoked the most high God: * and they kept not his testimonies.
<n>77:57</n> And they turned away, and kept not the covenant: * even like their fathers they were turned aside as a crooked bow.
<n>77:58</n> They provoked him to anger on their hills: * and moved him to jealousy with their graven things.
07.1e83c6e427:
<n>77:59</n> Audívit Deus, et sprevit: * et ad níhilum redégit valde Israël.
<n>77:60</n> Et répulit tabernáculum Silo: * tabernáculum suum, ubi habitávit in homínibus.
<n>77:61</n> Et trádidit in captivitátem virtútem eórum: * et pulchritúdinem eórum in manus inimíci.
<n>77:62</n> Et conclúsit in gládio pópulum suum: * et hereditátem suam sprevit.
<n>77:63</n> Iúvenes eórum comédit ignis: * et vírgines eórum non sunt lamentátæ.
<n>77:64</n> Sacerdótes eórum in gládio cecidérunt: * et víduæ eórum non plorabántur.
<n>77:65</n> Et excitátus est tamquam dórmiens Dóminus: * tamquam potens crapulátus a vino.
<n>77:66</n> Et percússit inimícos suos in posterióra: * oppróbrium sempitérnum dedit illis.
<n>77:67</n> Et répulit tabernáculum Ioseph: * et tribum Éphraim non elégit.
<n>77:68</n> Sed elégit tribum Iuda, * montem Sion quem diléxit.
<n>77:69</n> Et ædificávit sicut unicórnium sanctifícium suum in terra, * quam fundávit in sǽcula.
<n>77:70</n> Et elégit David, servum suum, et sústulit eum de grégibus óvium: * de post fœtántes accépit eum,
<n>77:71</n> Páscere Iacob, servum suum, * et Israël, hereditátem suam:
<n>77:72</n> Et pavit eos in innocéntia cordis sui: * et in intelléctibus mánuum suárum dedúxit eos.
07.f8fa165f04:
<n>77:59</n> God heard, and despised them, * and he reduced Israel exceedingly as it were to nothing.
<n>77:60</n> And he put away the tabernacle of Silo, * his tabernacle where he dwelt among men.
<n>77:61</n> And he delivered their strength into captivity: * and their beauty into the hands of the enemy.
<n>77:62</n> And he shut up his people under the sword: * and he despised his inheritance.
<n>77:63</n> Fire consumed their young men: * and their maidens were not lamented.
<n>77:64</n> Their priests fell by the sword: * and their widows did not mourn.
<n>77:65</n> And the Lord was awaked as one out of sleep, * and like a mighty man that hath been surfeited with wine.
<n>77:66</n> And he smote his enemies on the hinder parts: * he put them to an everlasting reproach.
<n>77:67</n> And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph: * and chose not the tribe of Ephraim:
<n>77:68</n> But he chose the tribe of Juda, * mount Sion which he loved.
<n>77:69</n> And he built his sanctuary as of unicorns, in the land * which he founded for ever.
<n>77:70</n> And he chose his servant David, and took him from the flocks of sheep: * he brought him from following the ewes great with young,
<n>77:71</n> To feed Jacob his servant, * and Israel his inheritance.
<n>77:72</n> And he fed them in the innocence of his heart: * and conducted them by the skilfulness of his hands.
07.7133c0b241:
<n>78:1</n> Deus, venérunt gentes in hereditátem tuam, polluérunt templum sanctum tuum: * posuérunt Ierúsalem in pomórum custódiam.
<n>78:2</n> Posuérunt morticína servórum tuórum, escas volatílibus cæli: * carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
<n>78:3</n> Effudérunt sánguinem eórum tamquam aquam in circúitu Ierúsalem: * et non erat qui sepelíret.
<n>78:4</n> Facti sumus oppróbrium vicínis nostris: * subsannátio et illúsio his, qui in circúitu nostro sunt.
<n>78:5</n> Úsquequo, Dómine, irascéris in finem: * accendétur velut ignis zelus tuus?
<n>78:6</n> Effúnde iram tuam in gentes, quæ te non novérunt: * et in regna quæ nomen tuum non invocavérunt:
<n>78:7</n> Quia comedérunt Iacob: * et locum eius desolavérunt.
<n>78:8</n> Ne memíneris iniquitátum nostrárum antiquárum, cito antícipent nos misericórdiæ tuæ: * quia páuperes facti sumus nimis.
<n>78:9</n> Ádiuva nos, Deus, salutáris noster: et propter glóriam nóminis tui, Dómine, líbera nos: * et propítius esto peccátis nostris, propter nomen tuum:
<n>78:10</n> Ne forte dicant in géntibus: Ubi est Deus eórum? * et innotéscat in natiónibus coram óculis nostris.
<n>78:10</n> Últio sánguinis servórum tuórum, qui effúsus est: * intróeat in conspéctu tuo gémitus compeditórum.
<n>78:11</n> Secúndum magnitúdinem brácchii tui, * pósside fílios mortificatórum.
<n>78:12</n> Et redde vicínis nostris séptuplum in sinu eórum: * impropérium ipsórum, quod exprobravérunt tibi, Dómine.
<n>78:13</n> Nos autem pópulus tuus, et oves páscuæ tuæ, * confitébimur tibi in sǽculum.
<n>78:13</n> In generatiónem et generatiónem * annuntiábimus laudem tuam.
07.689229ccda:
<n>78:1</n> O God, the heathens are come into thy inheritance, they have defiled thy holy temple: * they have made Jerusalem as a place to keep fruit.
<n>78:2</n> They have given the dead bodies of thy servants to be meat for the fowls of the air: * the flesh of thy saints for the beasts of the earth.
<n>78:3</n> They have poured out their blood as water, round about Jerusalem, * and there was none to bury them.
<n>78:4</n> We are become a reproach to our neighbours: * a scorn and derision to them that are round about us.
<n>78:5</n> How long, O Lord, wilt thou be angry for ever: * shall thy zeal be kindled like a fire?
<n>78:6</n> Pour out thy wrath upon the nations that have not known thee: * and upon the kingdoms that have not called upon thy name.
<n>78:7</n> Because they have devoured Jacob; * and have laid waste his place.
<n>78:8</n> Remember not our former iniquities: let thy mercies speedily prevent us, * for we are become exceeding poor.
<n>78:9</n> Help us, O God, our saviour: and for the glory of thy name, O Lord, deliver us: * and forgive us our sins for thy name’s sake:
<n>78:10</n> Lest they should say among the Gentiles: Where is their God? * And let him be made known among the nations before our eyes,
<n>78:10</n> By the revenging the blood of thy servants, which hath been shed: * let the sighing of the prisoners come in before thee.
<n>78:11</n> According to the greatness of thy arm, * take possession of the children of them that have been put to death.
<n>78:12</n> And render to our neighbours sevenfold in their bosom: * the reproach wherewith they have reproached thee, O Lord.
<n>78:13</n> But we thy people, and the sheep of thy pasture, * will give thanks to thee for ever.
<n>78:13</n> We will shew forth thy praise, * unto generation and generation.
07.0b1a7b4d16:
<n>79:2</n> Qui regis Israël, inténde: * qui dedúcis velut ovem Ioseph.
<n>79:2</n> Qui sedes super Chérubim, * manifestáre coram Éphraim, Béniamin, et Manásse.
<n>79:3</n> Éxcita poténtiam tuam, et veni, * ut salvos fácias nos.
<n>79:4</n> Deus, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
<n>79:5</n> Dómine, Deus virtútum, * quoúsque irascéris super oratiónem servi tui?
<n>79:6</n> Cibábis nos pane lacrimárum: * et potum dabis nobis in lácrimis in mensúra?
<n>79:7</n> Posuísti nos in contradictiónem vicínis nostris: * et inimíci nostri subsannavérunt nos.
<n>79:8</n> Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
07.5fe0b0e504:
<n>79:2</n> Give ear, O thou that rulest Israel: * thou that leadest Joseph like a sheep.
<n>79:2</n> Thou that sittest upon the cherubims, * shine forth before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasses.
<n>79:3</n> Stir up thy might, and come * to save us.
<n>79:4</n> Convert us, O God: * and shew us thy face, and we shall be saved.
<n>79:5</n> O Lord God of hosts, * how long wilt thou be angry against the prayer of thy servant?
<n>79:6</n> How long wilt thou feed us with the bread of tears: * and give us for our drink tears in measure?
<n>79:7</n> Thou hast made us to be a contradiction to our neighbours: * and our enemies have scoffed at us.
<n>79:8</n> O God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
07.8a7c858024:
<n>79:9</n> Víneam de Ægýpto transtulísti: * eiecísti gentes, et plantásti eam.
<n>79:10</n> Dux itíneris fuísti in conspéctu eius: * plantásti radíces eius, et implévit terram.
<n>79:11</n> Opéruit montes umbra eius: * et arbústa eius cedros Dei.
<n>79:12</n> Exténdit pálmites suos usque ad mare: * et usque ad flumen propágines eius.
<n>79:13</n> Ut quid destruxísti macériam eius: * et vindémiant eam omnes, qui prætergrediúntur viam?
<n>79:14</n> Exterminávit eam aper de silva: * et singuláris ferus depástus est eam.
<n>79:15</n> Deus virtútum, convértere: * réspice de cælo, et vide, et vísita víneam istam.
<n>79:16</n> Et pérfice eam, quam plantávit déxtera tua: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
<n>79:17</n> Incénsa igni, et suffóssa * ab increpatióne vultus tui períbunt.
<n>79:18</n> Fiat manus tua super virum déxteræ tuæ: * et super fílium hóminis, quem confirmásti tibi.
<n>79:19</n> Et non discédimus a te, vivificábis nos: * et nomen tuum invocábimus.
<n>79:20</n> Dómine, Deus virtútum, convérte nos: * et osténde fáciem tuam, et salvi érimus.
07.8ba8f9e506:
<n>79:9</n> Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt: * thou hast cast out the Gentiles and planted it.
<n>79:10</n> Thou wast the guide of its journey in its sight: * thou plantedst the roots thereof, and it filled the land.
<n>79:11</n> The shadow of it covered the hills: * and the branches thereof the cedars of God.
<n>79:12</n> It stretched forth its branches unto the sea, * and its boughs unto the river.
<n>79:13</n> Why hast thou broken down the hedge thereof, * so that all they who pass by the way do pluck it?
<n>79:14</n> The boar out of the wood hath laid it waste: * and a singular wild beast hath devoured it.
<n>79:15</n> Turn again, O God of hosts, * look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard:
<n>79:16</n> And perfect the same which thy right hand hath planted: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
<n>79:17</n> Things set on fire and dug down * shall perish at the rebuke of thy countenance.
<n>79:18</n> Let thy hand be upon the man of thy right hand: * and upon the son of man whom thou hast confirmed for thyself.
<n>79:19</n> And we depart not from thee, thou shalt quicken us: * and we will call upon thy name.
<n>79:20</n> O Lord God of hosts, convert us: * and shew thy face, and we shall be saved.
07.5b0f1877ce:
<n>76:2</n> Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * voce mea ad Deum, et inténdit mihi.
<n>76:3</n> In die tribulatiónis meæ Deum exquisívi, mánibus meis nocte contra eum: * et non sum decéptus.
<n>76:4</n> Rénuit consolári ánima mea, * memor fui Dei, et delectátus sum, et exercitátus sum: et defécit spíritus meus.
<n>76:5</n> Anticipavérunt vigílias óculi mei: * turbátus sum, et non sum locútus.
<n>76:6</n> Cogitávi dies antíquos: * et annos ætérnos in mente hábui.
<n>76:7</n> Et meditátus sum nocte cum corde meo, * et exercitábar, et scopébam spíritum meum.
<n>76:8</n> Numquid in ætérnum proíciet Deus: * aut non appónet ut complacítior sit adhuc?
<n>76:9</n> Aut in finem misericórdiam suam abscíndet, * a generatióne in generatiónem?
<n>76:10</n> Aut obliviscétur miseréri Deus? * aut continébit in ira sua misericórdias suas?
<n>76:11</n> Et dixi: Nunc cœpi: * hæc mutátio déxteræ Excélsi.
<n>76:12</n> Memor fui óperum Dómini: * quia memor ero ab inítio mirabílium tuórum.
<n>76:13</n> Et meditábor in ómnibus opéribus tuis: * et in adinventiónibus tuis exercébor.
07.890d2f8389:
<n>76:2</n> I cried to the Lord with my voice; * to God with my voice, and he gave ear to me.
<n>76:3</n> In the day of my trouble I sought God, with my hands lifted up to him in the night, * and I was not deceived.
<n>76:4</n> My soul refused to be comforted: * I remembered God, and was delighted, and was exercised, and my spirit swooned away.
<n>76:5</n> My eyes prevented the watches: * I was troubled, and I spoke not.
<n>76:6</n> I thought upon the days of old: * and I had in my mind the eternal years.
<n>76:7</n> And I meditated in the night with my own heart: * and I was exercised and I swept my spirit.
<n>76:8</n> Will God then cast off for ever? * or will he never be more favourable again?
<n>76:9</n> Or will he cut off his mercy for ever, * from generation to generation?
<n>76:10</n> Or will God forget to shew mercy? * or will he in his anger shut up his mercies?
<n>76:11</n> And I said, Now have I begun: * this is the change of the right hand of the most High.
<n>76:12</n> I remembered the works of the Lord: * for I will be mindful of thy wonders from the beginning.
<n>76:13</n> And I will meditate on all thy works: * and will be employed in thy inventions.
07.3e12c16d23:
<n>76:14</n> Deus, in sancto via tua: quis Deus magnus sicut Deus noster? * tu es Deus qui facis mirabília.
<n>76:15</n> Notam fecísti in pópulis virtútem tuam: * redemísti in brácchio tuo pópulum tuum, fílios Iacob et Ioseph.
<n>76:17</n> Vidérunt te aquæ, Deus, vidérunt te aquæ: * et timuérunt, et turbátæ sunt abýssi.
<n>76:18</n> Multitúdo sónitus aquárum: * vocem dedérunt nubes.
<n>76:18</n> Étenim sagíttæ tuæ tránseunt: * vox tonítrui tui in rota.
<n>76:19</n> Illuxérunt coruscatiónes tuæ orbi terræ: * commóta est, et contrémuit terra.
<n>76:20</n> In mari via tua, et sémitæ tuæ in aquis multis: * et vestígia tua non cognoscéntur.
<n>76:21</n> Deduxísti sicut oves pópulum tuum, * in manu Móysi et Aaron.
07.482f4257e1:
<n>76:14</n> Thy way, O God, is in the holy place: who is the great God like our God? * Thou art the God that dost wonders.
<n>76:15</n> Thou hast made thy power known among the nations: * with thy arm thou hast redeemed thy people, the children of Jacob and of Joseph.
<n>76:17</n> The waters saw thee, O God, the waters saw thee: * and they were afraid, and the depths were troubled.
<n>76:18</n> Great was the noise of the waters: * the clouds sent out a sound.
<n>76:18</n> For thy arrows pass: * the voice of thy thunder in a wheel.
<n>76:19</n> Thy lightnings enlightened the world: * the earth shook and trembled.
<n>76:20</n> Thy way is in the sea, and thy paths in many waters: * and thy footsteps shall not be known.
<n>76:21</n> Thou hast conducted thy people like sheep, * by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
07.eb3f7ee194:
<n>71:2</n> Deus, iudícium tuum regi da: * et iustítiam tuam fílio regis:
<n>71:2</n> Iudicáre pópulum tuum in iustítia, * et páuperes tuos in iudício.
<n>71:3</n> Suscípiant montes pacem pópulo: * et colles iustítiam.
<n>71:4</n> Iudicábit páuperes pópuli, et salvos fáciet fílios páuperum: * et humiliábit calumniatórem.
<n>71:5</n> Et permanébit cum sole, et ante lunam, * in generatióne et generatiónem.
<n>71:6</n> Descéndet sicut plúvia in vellus: * et sicut stillicídia stillántia super terram.
<n>71:7</n> Oriétur in diébus eius iustítia, et abundántia pacis: * donec auferátur luna.
<n>71:8</n> Et dominábitur a mari usque ad mare: * et a flúmine usque ad términos orbis terrárum.
<n>71:9</n> Coram illo prócident Æthíopes: * et inimíci eius terram lingent.
<n>71:10</n> Reges Tharsis, et ínsulæ múnera ófferent: * reges Árabum et Saba dona addúcent.
<n>71:11</n> Et adorábunt eum omnes reges terræ: * omnes gentes sérvient ei:
<n>71:12</n> Quia liberábit páuperem a poténte: * et páuperem, cui non erat adiútor.
<n>71:13</n> Parcet páuperi et ínopi: * et ánimas páuperum salvas fáciet.
<n>71:14</n> Ex usúris et iniquitáte rédimet ánimas eórum: * et honorábile nomen eórum coram illo.
<n>71:15</n> Et vivet, et dábitur ei de auro Arábiæ, et adorábunt de ipso semper: * tota die benedícent ei.
<n>71:16</n> Et erit firmaméntum in terra in summis móntium, superextollétur super Líbanum fructus eius: * et florébunt de civitáte sicut fænum terræ.
<n>71:17</n> Sit nomen eius benedíctum in sǽcula: * ante solem pérmanet nomen eius.
<n>71:17</n> Et benedicéntur in ipso omnes tribus terræ: * omnes gentes magnificábunt eum.
<n>71:18</n> Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, * qui facit mirabília solus:
<n>71:19</n> Et benedíctum nomen maiestátis eius in ætérnum: * et replébitur maiestáte eius omnis terra: fiat, fiat.
07.b4660b49d7:
<n>71:2</n> Give to the king thy judgment, O God: * and to the king’s son thy justice:
<n>71:2</n> To judge thy people with justice, * and thy poor with judgment.
<n>71:3</n> Let the mountains receive peace for the people: * and the hills justice.
<n>71:4</n> He shall judge the poor of the people, and he shall save the children of the poor: * and he shall humble the oppressor.
<n>71:5</n> And he shall continue with the sun, and before the moon, * throughout all generations.
<n>71:6</n> He shall come down like rain upon the fleece; * and as showers falling gently upon the earth.
<n>71:7</n> In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, * till the moon be taken away.
<n>71:8</n> And he shall rule from sea to sea, * and from the river unto the ends of the earth.
<n>71:9</n> Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down: * and his enemies shall lick the ground.
<n>71:10</n> The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents: * the kings of the Arabians and of Saba shall bring gifts:
<n>71:11</n> And all kings of the earth shall adore him: * all nations shall serve him.
<n>71:12</n> For he shall deliver the poor from the mighty: * and the needy that had no helper.
<n>71:13</n> He shall spare the poor and needy: * and he shall save the souls of the poor.
<n>71:14</n> He shall redeem their souls from usuries and iniquity: * and their names shall be honourable in his sight.
<n>71:15</n> And he shall live, and to him shall be given of the gold of Arabia, for him they shall always adore: * they shall bless him all the day.
<n>71:16</n> And there shall be a firmament on the earth on the tops of mountains, above Libanus shall the fruit thereof be exalted: * and they of the city shall flourish like the grass of the earth.
<n>71:17</n> Let his name be blessed for evermore: * his name continueth before the sun.
<n>71:17</n> And in him shall all the tribes of the earth be blessed: * all nations shall magnify him.
<n>71:18</n> Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, * who alone doth wonderful things.
<n>71:19</n> And blessed be the name of his majesty for ever: * and the whole earth shall be filled with his majesty. So be it. So be it.
